title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Construction Set. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Construction Set
options.lineage: Architectural construction documents: title blocks, building sections, schedules, detail sheets
options.thesis: Your career issued as a drawing set: the stack is a building section and every shipped product is a room in it.
materials: Plotted bond sheet in light theme, cyanotype blueprint in dark: one drawing, two reproduction processes
Flat poché fills from Le Corbusier's architectural polychromy, material hatch patterns, leader-line callouts
options.viewport: A full-width section drawing of your stack: Interface, Mobile, Services, and Data floors, with rooms tagged by real products (GoRuck, the clinical-study app, hivetracks, Expertise journeys). Your name sits in the title block, with an 'Issued for hire' stamp and the contact action beside it.
options.risk: Slides into blueprint cliché if it goes blue-and-white. It has to stay a plotted, colored set that uses real drawing conventions.

raised.raise: Recency as line weight: current work is drawn as heavy new construction and older roles step down to lighter existing lines, so the sheet reads newest-darkest at a glance.
One reserved ink: redline marks only what is live (the current role, the availability stamp, the selected floor, focus). Nothing decorative is ever red.
Isolate and dim: selecting a floor, role, or project isolates its linework and drops the rest of the sheet to gray underlay.
Depth by flat overlap only: poché fields and stacked sheets layer as flat color. No shadows, glows, gradients, or glass anywhere.
One drafting tempo: every draw-on and reveal runs on a single shared beat, so the motion reads as one plotter pen rather than scattered effects.
One continuous run: a single dimension string runs from 2018 to the present, so the career reads as one unbroken line.

options.label: Press Proof
options.lineage: Offset pre-press proof sheets: color bars, registration targets, crop marks
options.thesis: Every project pulled as a press proof. Craft is shown as registration: misaligned process layers snap into register as you read.
materials: Uncoated proof stock with process-color overprints
Registration targets, crop marks, color-bar strips as live UI
options.viewport: Your name as an oversized four-color overprint, slightly out of register, that locks into register on load. Color bars are the nav and the first project plate is already in the frame.
options.risk: Print-production motifs are a familiar move in design portfolios, and full CMYK can turn loud. This is where many runs in the category land.

options.label: Orienteering Course
options.lineage: ISOM orienteering maps and control descriptions
options.thesis: Your career as a course: numbered controls from Alliance to MountainDev, overprinted in purple on the terrain.
options.viewport: A contour map with the purple course running from 2018 to the present, each control a role.
options.case: Fuses cleanly, but hiring managers don't recognize orienteering, and the course can't explain 'full stack' or craft.
options.kept: One reserved ink, used only for the active path.
options.risk: Reads as a hobby theme, not a professional record.

options.label: Event Display
options.thesis: Your skills as tracks bursting from one collision.
options.viewport: A ring section with tech tracks curving outward from your name.
options.case: Fuses into the neon-on-black look your stash already tried, and it buries the real product work.
options.risk: Near-black plus neon is the most common AI portfolio look.

options.label: Layered Papercut
options.thesis: The stack as layers of cut colored paper pasted one over another.
options.viewport: A symmetric roundel whose layers are your stack.
options.case: Layers map neatly to the stack, but a folk-craft world doesn't read as a hire-me engineering portfolio.
options.kept: Depth by flat overlap only, never by shadow.

options.label: Ink Basin
options.thesis: The page as a live fluid surface that answers the pointer.
options.viewport: A marbling basin with your name held in a still margin.
options.case: Beautiful, but a GPU fluid solver is the heavy, effect-led page you ruled out, and it says nothing about your work.
options.kept: Newest ink is darkest: recency encoded as intensity.
options.risk: Slow on mid-range phones. Art piece, not portfolio.

options.label: Neon Circuit
options.thesis: Your name bent as one continuous glowing tube.
options.viewport: A dark room with your name igniting in cobalt neon.
options.case: Glow on dark is the cluster to avoid, and neon has nothing to say about shipping software.
options.kept: One continuous run threading the whole piece.

options.label: Rubber-Hose Cel
options.thesis: Sections arrive through an iris like gags in a cartoon.
options.viewport: Your name in fat outlined lettering inside an oval iris.
options.case: Playful, but it undercuts high-stakes products like a clinical-study app.
options.kept: Motion on one rhythm rather than scattered curves.
options.risk: Gimmick reading for a hiring audience.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The modern developer portfolio, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Big name and title centered, two buttons, then a bento grid of projects.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of developer portfolios, by design.
